bge-000-1.q: Why have philosophers so often failed to find the truth?
Haven't the great philosophical systems given us solid foundations that still stand?
Is it fair to say that most grand philosophical systems are just old superstitions and grammar tricks in disguise?

bge-000-2.q: What has the long struggle against Platonism and Christianity given Europe?
Does the free press, with its endless newspapers and information, relieve the strain on the modern spirit?
What does it mean to be a "good European"?

bge-001-1.q: Why should we value the will to truth at all?
Why are we so desperate for the truth? Wouldn't ignorance sometimes serve us better?
I want to know the truth about myself, even if it hurts. But why do I want that?

bge-002-1.q: Can something valuable arise out of its opposite, or must every good thing have a pure origin?
Honesty and deceit are opposites. Surely selflessness can't grow out of selfishness?
Could our best qualities be secretly tangled up with our worst impulses?

bge-003-1.q: How much of philosophical thinking is really instinct?
Are our supposedly rational beliefs driven by hidden needs of the body?
Logic is logic. How can reasoning possibly be shaped by instinct?

bge-004-1.q: Is the falseness of an opinion an objection to it?
Surely it is always better to believe what is true?
Could we need certain illusions in order to live at all?

bge-007-1.q: What did Epicurus think of Plato and his followers?
Why are philosophers so spiteful about each other?

bge-009-1.q: What is wrong with the Stoic ideal of living according to nature?
Isn't living in harmony with nature the wisest way to live?
Why do philosophies always describe the world as if it agreed with their own values?

bge-010-1.q: Why do so many thinkers today deny the reality of the world we see?
Are modern skeptics about reality really seeking truth, or are they escaping something?

bge-011-2.q: What is wrong with Kant's question about how synthetic judgments a priori are possible?
Kant answered by pointing to a faculty of the mind. Why isn't that good enough for you?

bge-012-1.q: What do you make of the soul? Should science give it up?
Is the idea of one unified, indivisible self outdated?
If the soul is not an indivisible unit, doesn't that simply mean it doesn't exist?

bge-013-1.q: Is self-preservation the basic drive of living things?
Do we act mainly to survive, or to express our strength?

bge-015-1.q: Are our sense organs the cause of the outer world, or the other way round?
Some idealists say the external world is merely the product of our organs of perception. Is that persuasive?

bge-016-1.q: Descartes said "I think, therefore I am" is beyond doubt. Why do you disagree?
When I say "I am thinking," what am I actually assuming?

bge-017-1.q: Who does the thinking: "I", or something else?
Thoughts often pop into my head unbidden. Does that mean I am not their author?

bge-019-2.q: Why do people believe that the will is free?
Why do I feel so powerful when I decide to do something and then succeed?
What is the harm in believing that willing is enough to cause an action?

bge-019-3.q: How would you describe the true nature of willing?
What is morality really about, at bottom?

bge-021-1.q: If free will is absurd, doesn't that mean we are all just puppets of determinism?
When we blame ourselves or others, are we assuming a kind of freedom that doesn't exist?

bge-021-2.q: Why do people argue so fiercely over whether the will is free?
Isn't it compassionate to say that criminals are not responsible for what they've done?
Are people who deny free will just trying to dodge responsibility?

bge-023-1.q: What must psychology dare to do that it has not yet done?
Could envy and hatred actually serve life rather than damage it?
Isn't morality the very thing that keeps us from becoming worse people?

bge-024-1.q: Why does knowledge depend on ignorance?
Do we live in a simplified, falsified world? How much of what seems clear to me is invented?
Isn't the love of truth the opposite of the love of error?

bge-025-1.q: Should a philosopher be willing to suffer for the truth?
Is it wise to publicly fight for what you believe, or is it better to keep quiet?
What is your view of solitude?

bge-025-2.q: What does martyrdom do to a philosopher?
Doesn't suffering for the truth prove that a thinker is sincere?

bge-026-2.q: Why should a lover of knowledge listen to those who speak crudely of human nature without indignation?
Are cynics more honest than idealists?
Isn't the indignant person morally superior to the cynic?

bge-028-1.q: Why is translation from one language to another so difficult?
I read philosophy in translation. What am I missing?

bge-030-1.q: Why do the deepest insights sound like folly to the uninitiated?
Shouldn't knowledge be available to everyone equally?
Can a book be harmful to one reader and helpful to another?

bge-031-1.q: Why is the taste for the unconditional such a bad taste?
In my twenties I was passionately certain about everything; now I cringe. Is that normal?

bge-032-1.q: How did people come to judge actions by their origin rather than their consequences?
Should we judge people by their intentions or by the results of what they do?
Isn't the intention behind an act what makes it moral?

bge-032-2.q: Is intention the true measure of an action's value?
If we abandon the morality of intentions, what could possibly replace it?
What would it mean to go "beyond" morality?

bge-035-1.q: Should one seek the truth in order to do good?
Is the pursuit of truth compatible with wanting to help humanity?

bge-036-1.q: What is the methodological argument for explaining the world through a single kind of causality?
Isn't the will merely a psychological illusion rather than a force in the world?

bge-036-2.q: What is the world when seen from within?
Is there one principle underlying all our drives and all living things?

bge-037-1.q: If God is disproved, is the devil disproved too?
Do you believe in the devil?

bge-038-1.q: How do later ages misunderstand the past?
Do we misinterpret history to make it bearable? The French Revolution, for example?

bge-039-1.q: Does it prove a doctrine true that it makes people happy or virtuous?
A truth that makes people miserable and bad can't be worth pursuing, can it?
How much truth can a person actually endure?

bge-041-1.q: How does one test one's own independence?
I feel deeply attached to my country, my career and my ideals. Is it wrong to hold on so tightly?
Isn't sympathy for suffering people something we should cling to?

bge-042-1.q: What kind of philosophers do you see coming, and what do you call them?

bge-043-1.q: Will the philosophers of the future be friends of the truth? Will they be dogmatists?
Shouldn't a good idea be one that everyone can share? What is wrong with a "common good"?
I feel uneasy when my opinions match everyone else's. Is that a healthy instinct?

bge-044-2.q: Under what conditions has the human being grown strongest?
Wouldn't a safe and comfortable world bring out the best in humanity?
Did hardship make you who you are? Do we need danger and difficulty to grow?

bge-044-3.q: What kind of people are the free spirits?
Describe yourself and your kind in a few lines.
I love solitude and I'm curious about everything, sometimes to a fault. Is that a philosopher's temperament?

bge-045-1.q: What is the great hunting-ground of the psychologist?
Why does deep understanding of the human soul demand so much personal experience?
Why is your curiosity such a pleasant vice?

bge-046-1.q: What was the Christian faith at its beginnings, and what did it demand?
Wasn't early Christianity a gentle religion of love and mercy?
Why does "God on the Cross" sound so ordinary to us but was so shocking at the time?

bge-047-1.q: What do solitude, fasting and abstinence have to do with religious neurosis?
Is religious experience just a matter of the body and its excesses?
Isn't the saint the proof that human beings can truly deny their own will?

bge-047-2.q: Why has the saint fascinated men and philosophers of every age?
Can a bad person suddenly become a good person, or is that a trick of interpretation?

bge-051-1.q: Why did the mightiest men bow before the saint?
Why do powerful people respect those who give up everything?

bge-052-1.q: What do you think of the Old and New Testaments?
Isn't the New Testament the more refined and moral of the two books?
Should the two Testaments have been bound together as a single book?

bge-053-1.q: People are becoming less religious, yet many still feel a religious pull. What is going on?
Isn't science what killed the belief in God?

bge-054-1.q: What does modern philosophy do to the Christian doctrine of the soul?
Descartes started from the thinking self. Isn't that the firmest ground we have?
Is the "I" the source of thought, or just a product of it?

bge-055-1.q: What are the three rungs of religious cruelty?
How can giving up God be a form of cruelty toward oneself?

bge-056-1.q: What is the opposite ideal to pessimism?
Would you want to live your life again exactly as it was, forever?
Isn't Schopenhauer right that life is mostly suffering and the wise man should renounce the will?

bge-057-1.q: Will our grand notions of God and sin one day seem like children's toys?
Will the problems that torment us now seem trivial to future generations?

bge-058-1.q: What does a religious life need in order to flourish?
Is busyness and modern hard work the enemy of faith?
Aren't people today simply too rational to believe?

bge-058-2.q: How does the modern scholar treat religion?
Isn't tolerance toward religion a virtue in a scholar?
Why do academics tend to look down on believers without noticing their own naivete?

bge-050-1.q: What forms does the passion for God take?
Isn't Protestantism a purer, more sincere form of faith than the Catholic kind?

bge-059-1.q: What wisdom lies in the fact that men are superficial?
Is religion a kind of art, a beautiful falsification of life?
Isn't piety just a sincere response to the mystery of existence?

bge-060-1.q: What is the noblest sentiment mankind has reached?
Why can't love for mankind stand on its own, without any higher purpose behind it?

bge-061-1.q: How does the philosopher use religion?
Can religion serve as a tool of rulers, and of self-discipline for those who rule?
Isn't religion a private matter of faith rather than a tool of education and government?

bge-061-2.q: What does religion give to ordinary people?
Is religion an opiate that makes people content with their lot?

bge-062-1.q: What are the dangers when religion rules instead of serving as a tool in the philosopher's hands?
Isn't it a virtue that Christianity and Buddhism care for the suffering and the weak?
Does compassion for those who fail keep humanity from improving?

bge-062-2.q: What has Christianity done to Europe?
Christianity gave Europe comfort, charity and hospitals. How can you call that a bad thing?
Why do you call Christianity the most portentous of presumptions?

bge-062-3.q: How did "equality before God" shape the European of today?
Has modern society produced a comfortable, gregarious, mediocre type of person?

bge-064-1.q: Is "knowledge for its own sake" a moral ideal?
Isn't the pursuit of knowledge for its own sake the most innocent thing a person can do?

bge-066-1.q: Why does a person allow himself to be exploited and deceived?
Is being a doormat a sign of divinity?

bge-068-1.q: What happens when memory and pride disagree?
I remember doing something embarrassing, but I keep insisting to myself it wasn't me. Why do I do that?

bge-071-1.q: What must the sage do to see truly as an astronomer?
What do the stars teach us about looking up?

bge-077-1.q: What do people want from their principles?
Two people can hold the same beliefs and be completely different. Why?

bge-079-1.q: What does a soul reveal when it knows it is loved but does not love in return?
Someone loves me deeply, and I feel nothing but a little annoyance. What does that say about me?

bge-080-1.q: Does explaining something make it lose its power over us?

bge-085-1.q: Why do men and women misunderstand each other?
Why do my partner and I keep misunderstanding each other even though we feel the same things?

bge-087-1.q: How can a person hold his heart captive and yet keep his spirit free?
I keep my feelings under tight control, and my thinking is freer for it. Is that a good bargain?

bge-090-1.q: Why do heavy, melancholy men grow lighter through hatred and love?
I get strangely energized when I'm angry or in love, even though I'm usually gloomy. Why?

bge-091-1.q: Why do people mistake a cold man for a burning one?
Tell me about someone so cold he burns.

bge-093-1.q: Is affability a sign of love for mankind?
The friendliest people I know seem to hold everyone in secret contempt. Is that possible?

bge-095-1.q: What comes after being ashamed of one's immorality?
Is guilt over doing wrong a step toward doubting morality itself?

bge-100-1.q: Why do we pretend to ourselves that we are simpler than we are?
Why do I present a simpler version of myself to the people around me?

bge-102-1.q: Should a lover be flattered or disenchanted to learn that his love is returned?
Why do lovers doubt the one who loves them back?

bge-103-1.q: What is the danger in happiness?
Everything's going right for me and I'm oddly uneasy. Why?

bge-105-1.q: Why does the free spirit dislike pious fraud more than impious fraud?
Isn't a free spirit supposed to be free of all such loyalties?

bge-107-1.q: Is it a sign of strong character to ignore counter-arguments once a decision is made?
When I have made a decision, I refuse to hear any advice against it. Is that strength or stubbornness?

bge-110-1.q: Why are the defenders of a criminal so seldom artists?
Shouldn't a criminal's advocate simply argue the facts?

bge-112-1.q: Why do contemplative men find believers too noisy?
I prefer to think things over quietly, and loud, certain people exhaust me. Is that a philosopher's temperament?

bge-114-1.q: How does the expectation of sexual love spoil the prospects of women?
Isn't it natural to expect a great deal from love?

bge-116-1.q: What marks the great epochs of our lives?
Is there a moment when we learn to see what we thought was our worst side as our best?

bge-118-1.q: What is the innocence of admiration?
Why does admiring someone feel so pure?

bge-120-1.q: Why is love that grows too quickly out of sensuality so fragile?
My relationship began with intense attraction, and it feels like it's already coming apart. Why?

bge-122-1.q: Is rejoicing in praise a form of vanity?
Isn't it vain to enjoy being praised?

bge-125-1.q: Why do we blame others when they force us to change our opinion of them?
My friend surprised me by acting out of character, and I'm angry at them for it. Is that fair?

bge-126-1.q: Say something cutting about nations and great men.

bge-127-1.q: Why is science hostile to modesty in the eyes of women?
Isn't science equally open to everyone regardless of sex?

bge-129-1.q: Why is the devil the oldest friend of knowledge?
What would the devil think of God?

bge-130-1.q: When does a person's real self begin to show?
What does it say about someone when they stop performing what they're good at?

bge-131-1.q: Why do the sexes deceive themselves about each other?
Aren't men and women equally capable of honesty and peace?

bge-135-1.q: Is Pharisaism a corruption of goodness?
Isn't hypocrisy always a failing of the good man?

bge-136-1.q: Some friends help me think, and others need my help. Which makes for a better relationship?

bge-138-1.q: Do we invent the people we talk with?
Do I actually know my friends, or just my mental image of them?

bge-143-1.q: Where do many systems of morals come from?
Do we pass off our strengths as our hardest struggles?

bge-144-1.q: Is there a connection between scholarship and sexual nature in women?
Isn't intellectual achievement independent of sex?

bge-145-1.q: Does woman's genius for adornment come from her instinct for the secondary role?
Why should any woman accept a secondary role?

bge-148-1.q: Who is better than women at persuading others to think well of them?
Aren't men just as good at that trick?

bge-150-1.q: What happens around a hero, a demigod, and a God?
What becomes of the world around God?

bge-152-1.q: Where there is the tree of knowledge, is there always Paradise?
Are the serpents right about the tree?

bge-157-1.q: Is the thought of suicide a consolation?
I find myself thinking about ending it all on bad nights, and somehow it helps me sleep. What should I make of that?

bge-163-1.q: Does love reveal the true character of a lover?
My partner seems so much better when they're in love with me. Is that their real self?

bge-164-1.q: What did Jesus say about the law and morals?
Wasn't Jesus a great moral teacher?

bge-165-1.q: Why does a shepherd need a bell-wether?
What does a leader need from the herd?

bge-172-1.q: Why must one never confess that one embraces someone out of love for mankind?
I love humanity in the abstract but find individuals difficult. Is that normal?

bge-174-1.q: Do utilitarians really love the useful?
Isn't utility the plainest and most honest guide for how to act?

bge-179-1.q: Do the consequences of our actions care that we have reformed?
I've changed a lot, but my past still follows me. Why doesn't it let go?

bge-186-1.q: Why is the science of morals so immature compared to moral feeling?
Philosophers have laid moral foundations for centuries. Hasn't the job been done?
Can we study morality the way we study nature, by comparing different peoples and ages?

bge-187-1.q: What do systems of morals really tell us about their authors?
Kant said there is a categorical imperative in us all. Why doubt it?
Do my moral beliefs say more about me than about the world?

bge-188-1.q: Why is every system of morals a kind of tyranny, and why is that not an objection?
Freedom means being free of arbitrary rules. Why do you praise constraint?
Does creativity really need discipline, or does it come from letting go?

bge-188-2.q: How did the long bondage of the spirit educate Europe?
Wasn't the Church's control over thought purely harmful to human progress?
Do we need to obey someone for a long time before we can be free?

bge-189-1.q: Why did the English make Sunday so gloomy?
Do we need periods of restraint or fasting to sharpen our appetites?

bge-191-1.q: What is the old conflict between faith and knowledge, or instinct and reason?
Socrates put reason above everything. Wasn't he right?
Should I trust my gut or my reasoning when making a moral choice?

bge-192-1.q: Why are our senses slow to learn anything new?
Do we really see what's in front of us, or only what we expect to see?

bge-192-2.q: How much are we artists without knowing it?
In conversation, do I see the other person's face or invent it?

bge-193-1.q: How do our dreams shape our waking life?
I keep having flying dreams. Could they change what I think of as happiness?

bge-194-1.q: What does it mean to possess something one desires?
How much do I want to be truly known by the person I love, rather than merely admired?
Isn't possession a matter of simple ownership, without any of this psychology?

bge-195-1.q: What was the role of the Jewish prophets in the history of morals?
Wasn't the inversion of values a moral improvement of humanity?

bge-197-1.q: Why have moralists misunderstood beasts and men of prey?
Are the ruthless, powerful people we despise maybe just healthier than the rest of us?
Isn't a man like Cesare Borgia simply a criminal?

bge-198-1.q: What are moral systems that promise happiness really worth?
Aren't the Stoics and Spinoza wise to teach mastery over the emotions?
Is most self-help advice just expediency and stupidity dressed as wisdom?

bge-199-1.q: Why does the herd need to obey?
Today's politicians claim to be servants of the people. Are they hiding a bad conscience about commanding?
Aren't kindness, modesty and public spirit real virtues rather than herd traits?

bge-199-2.q: Why do gregarious Europeans welcome an absolute ruler like Napoleon?
Why do people in democracies sometimes long for a strongman?

bge-200-1.q: What kind of man does an age of dissolution and mixed inheritance produce?
I feel torn between contradictory drives and values. Is that weakness or a source of strength?
Isn't peace and inner unity the highest happiness a person can reach?

bge-201-1.q: How did morality of love for one's neighbour arise?
Isn't compassion a natural moral instinct that has always been with us?
Is fear of others the real origin of moral rules?

bge-202-1.q: Why do you call European morality herd morality?
Isn't it arrogant to say that all Europe shares a mere herd instinct?
Is democracy the modern heir of Christianity?

bge-203-1.q: Where should the hopes of those who distrust democracy be fixed?
Do we need new leaders and philosophers to break humanity out of history's blind drift?
Isn't democracy the best safeguard against tyranny and folly?

bge-203-2.q: What is the greatest danger you see for mankind?
Are we heading toward a mediocre humanity of equal rights and equal claims?
What is a new mission worth?

bge-204-1.q: Why should science not rule over philosophy?
Science has proven itself far more reliable than philosophy. Why shouldn't it take the lead?
Why do scientists so often dismiss philosophy with such confidence?

bge-204-2.q: What causes young scholars to scorn philosophy?
Wasn't Schopenhauer right to attack Hegel?
Did the personal failings of modern philosophers damage philosophy's reputation?

bge-204-3.q: What has become of philosophy in our time?
Has philosophy shrunk into a theory of knowledge that never leaves the threshold?
Can a philosophy that denies itself the right to enter ever rule?

bge-205-1.q: What dangers threaten the growth of a true philosopher today?
In an age of endless specialization, can anyone still be a philosopher?
Isn't a philosopher who doubts and hesitates simply a poor thinker?

bge-205-2.q: Why is the philosopher so often confused with the scholar or the saint?
People praise those who live "wisely" and apart from the fray. Is that true wisdom?
Does a real philosopher live wisely?

bge-206-1.q: What is the man of learning compared with the genius?
Why do scholars so often resent exceptional people?

bge-207-1.q: What is wrong with the objective man?
Is being purely objective, with no personal stake, something to aspire to?
A scientist should be a mirror of the facts. What is wrong with that?

bge-207-2.q: Can the objective man truly love or hate?
I've become so detached and even-handed that I struggle to feel strongly about anything. What is happening to me?
What's left of a man who mirrors everything?

bge-207-3.q: What is the objective man good for?
Isn't the objective scholar the pinnacle of intellectual life?

bge-208-1.q: Why does a philosopher who says he isn't a skeptic make people nervous?
Isn't skepticism the safest and most reasonable stance for a thinker?
Is skepticism sometimes just a way of avoiding commitment?

bge-208-2.q: What is skepticism a symptom of?
Modern life mixes classes, cultures and values constantly. Is that why so many of us feel paralyzed and unable to decide?
Isn't "I don't know" the honest answer to most big questions?

bge-209-1.q: What is a stronger kind of skepticism than the weak kind that comes from a broken will?
What did Frederick the Great's father fear about his son?

bge-210-1.q: Are the philosophers of the future skeptics, or something else?
Shouldn't a philosopher want the truth to be uplifting?
Why are you suspicious of ideas that inspire us simply because they inspire us?

bge-211-1.q: What is the difference between a philosophical worker and a real philosopher?
Are most academic philosophers mere workers who organize other people's ideas?
Isn't understanding the past a great task in itself?

bge-214-1.q: Is having a good conscience just wearing our grandparents' pigtail?

bge-215-1.q: Why are our actions determined by more than one morality?
I feel pulled in different moral directions at once. Is that a defect or just the modern condition?

bge-217-1.q: Why should we be careful with people who pride themselves on moral tact?
A friend who once misjudged me can't seem to forgive me for it. Why?

bge-218-1.q: What should psychologists study instead of bourgeois stupidity?
Good, honest, ordinary people mean well. Why call their mediocrity cunning?
Why does mediocrity seem to gang up on exceptional people?

bge-219-1.q: Why do the intellectually shallow love to judge morally?
People who moralize constantly online seem to be compensating for something. Is that right?
Isn't honesty and respectability worth more than sophistication of mind?

bge-220-1.q: Is there really such a thing as a disinterested action?
A mother sacrificing herself for her child is surely acting without self-interest. Isn't she?
When I make a sacrifice for someone, do I always get something out of it?

bge-222-1.q: What does the preaching of sympathy reveal about the preachers?
Does all the talk about empathy today hide a deeper dissatisfaction with ourselves?
Isn't sympathy the most basic of human virtues?

bge-223-1.q: Why does the modern European need history as a storeroom of costumes?
We keep trying on new styles and identities and none of them fit. Why?
Will our laughter have a future?

bge-224-1.q: What is the historical sense, and where does it come from?
Does having access to every culture's past make us richer or shallower?
Why can we enjoy Homer when the French classicists couldn't?

bge-224-2.q: Why is the historical sense a mark of bad taste?
Isn't it a virtue to appreciate every age and culture equally?
Why do we love Shakespeare's wild mixture of high and low that a stricter culture would have rejected?

bge-224-3.q: Is our love of the infinite in conflict with good taste?
Are we modern people drawn to danger and excess because we've lost a sense of proportion?

bge-225-1.q: What is wrong with measuring the worth of things by pleasure and pain?
Isn't the reduction of suffering the noblest goal a person can pursue?
Does great suffering shape people and make them greater?

bge-225-2.q: What do you mean by "sympathy against sympathy"?
How can withholding sympathy ever be a form of sympathy?

bge-226-1.q: What kind of duties do the immoralists have?

bge-227-1.q: Which virtue is left to the free spirits?
Can honesty become a vice, or a form of vanity?
Why do you warn against becoming saints and bores?

bge-228-1.q: Why has moral philosophy been so tedious?
The English utilitarians simply wanted the greatest happiness for the greatest number. What's wrong with that?
Why do so many discussions of ethics feel like sermons rather than real inquiry?

bge-229-1.q: What is the truth about cruelty in higher culture?
We have overcome our cruelty through civilization, haven't we?
Is the pleasure we take in tragedy and violent entertainment a disguised form of cruelty?

bge-229-2.q: Why do people enjoy tragedy, bull-fights and gladiatorial contests?
Can cruelty toward oneself be a source of pleasure, as in self-denial and religious asceticism?
Isn't the pursuit of knowledge the opposite of cruelty?

bge-230-1.q: What is the fundamental will of the spirit?
Why do we choose ignorance and narrow horizons sometimes even when we could know more?
Is the mind more like a stomach than a mirror?

bge-230-2.q: What is the cruelty of the intellectual conscience?
Are noble words like honesty and love of truth just a costume for human vanity?
Why not simply call this cruelty "extravagant honesty"?

bge-230-3.q: What does it mean to translate man back into nature?
Would it change how we treat each other if we saw ourselves as just another part of nature?

bge-231-1.q: What is the unteachable core within each thinker?
Do my strongest convictions say more about who I am than what is true?
What do you mean by "the great stupidity which we embody"?

bge-235-1.q: What piece of motherly wisdom did Madame de Lambert offer her son?
What advice would you give a young man about folly?

bge-236-1.q: What should we make of Goethe's line that the eternal feminine draws us aloft?
Does the eternally masculine draw women aloft, too?

bge-240-1.q: What is your impression of Wagner's Mastersingers overture?
What does Wagner's music tell us about the German character?
Why do you say Germans have no today?

bge-241-1.q: What is the difference between a great deed and a great thought?
A politician builds a huge empire and everyone calls him great. Is he?

bge-241-2.q: Is a statesman great who turns his people to national politics and narrows their souls?
Is being mad and strong the same as being great?
Isn't a leader who unites his people around national pride serving them well?

bge-242-1.q: What is happening physiologically as Europe becomes more democratic?
Will globalization and mobility create a rootless, adaptable humanity?
Isn't the leveling of classes and nations a straightforward moral gain?

bge-242-2.q: Does the democratizing of Europe prepare for tyrants?
Could a society of equals create the conditions for a strongman to rise?

bge-243-1.q: What do you hope men will do like the sun?

bge-244-1.q: Why is it so hard to define a national character like the German one?
What is the German soul like?

bge-245-2.q: What was Schumann's danger for German music?
Schumann's music was sincere and deeply felt. Why do you look down on it?

bge-246-1.q: Why do you say German books are a torture to a good reader?
